newsitem.title: UK: Quick thinking graduates sought by NatWest Markets.
newsitem.headline: Quick thinking graduates sought by NatWest Markets.

text.p: NatWest Markets is seeking fast-thinking graduates to join the firm just 48 hours after the dramatic resignation of its chief executive Martin Owen and embarking on a major strategic overhaul.

A half-page advertisement in Wednesday's Financial Times -- headlined "Investment banking is all about fast, informed decision-making" -- called for top graduates to apply to the investment banking arm of Britain's NatWest Bank.
Quick decision making is essential as applications must be in by June 27.
But the really ambitious -- or those who read their daily newspapers -- may be setting their sights rather higher, the firm is also seeking a new boss after Owen's sudden resignation on Monday.

His departure followed an embarrassing and costly episode in the firm's derivatives division earlier this year, resulting in a 77 million pound ($126.1 million) direct loss and a profit warning for its parent bank.

An independent probe into what went wrong in NatWest Markets' interest rate options operation over a two-year period is due to report by the end of the month. The affair has already led to the suspension of five managers at the firm.
The Bank of England and financial markets watchdog the Securities and Futures Authority (SFA) have been kept informed of developments and could chose to act as a result of the inquiry.

In its advert, NatWest Markets said it was seeking "top quality graduates" to join either its global equities and global financial markets, operations, information technology or credit risk divisions.

Despite Monday's announcement it would reconsider aspects of its investment banking strategy, NatWest Markets said in the advert it intended "entering the new millennium as a premier global, integrated investment bank". NatWest's chief executive Derek Wanless has temporarily taken over the reins at NatWest Markets until a replacement for Owen, either from inside or outside the firm, is found. ($ = 0.610 British Pounds)
